item.title: LATIN PARADISE SALSA & BACHATA MONTHLY PARTY — Fri Aug 14, 8:00 PM — Crofton Hall Orpington
item.description: Learn Salsa, learn Bachata! Have fun and meet new friends!​ Our regular Fridays become a party on the Second Friday of every month. Join us at our Bromley Special Salsa & Bachata Party, hosted at Bromley United Services Club, Bromley, with plenty of free street parking available. We kick off the night with Salsa & Bachata lessons. If you’re new to dancing, we recommend joining our beginners’ group. All levels are welcome! No prior experience or dance partner is needed. Many attendees come solo, and we rotate partners throughout the lesson, giving you the chance to dance with different people. If you’d prefer to stay with your own partner for the entire class, just let the teacher know, and we’ll be happy to accommodate you. Since most Latin parties feature both Salsa and Bachata, learning both is not only fun but also a must! So, we strongly recommend and encourage our students to learn both. SCHEDULE: 7pm to 8pm: Cuban Salsa: Beginners – Improvers – Intermediate 8pm to 9pm:

item.title: Leaders Choice: Bread & Butter to the Leslie St Spit — Wed Aug 19, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Bread & Butter to the Leslie St. Spit A easy rolling city spin starting in midtown, heading South and a little bit West meandering through residential streets to the lake. Then we’ll head East along the lakeshore, have a little visit with Biidaasigge park before going down to the spit for the turnaround. We will head back up Cherry St., with a coffee/ice cream stop at the Distillery, then head North up Bayview tackling the gradual yet long Bayview hill. Once at the top, we’ll meander back to the start point at Bread and Butter where you can enjoy lunch if you wish. Start time : 9:30 am Start and end : Meet at Bread & Butter Cafe , 507 Mount Pleasant Road Route : https://ridewithgps.com/route...

item.title: Frequency: Janel Jones + Atonal — Sat Aug 22, 8:00 PM — Worth Gallery
item.description: Join us for Frequency — a monthly live music series at Worth Gallery. Curated by our Sound Director Janel Jones. Frequency spotlights BIPOC musicians of varying genres through intimate, stripped-back shows. Celebrating sound, connection, and creative expression in Toronto's vibrant music scene. Find your new favorite musician in your new favorite gallery. This month we welcome back Janel Jones, who'll be crafting a special night of visual and sonic soundscapes with Atonal. Janel is a multi-disciplinary artist and songwriter whose practice centers healing, reflection, and play through sound. Rooted in jazz, soul, and contemporary improvisation, Janel's sound is shaped by their Carribean heritage and over a decade performing within Toronto's music community. Their music honors the ancestors, and holds the complexities of their intersectional earth experience. item.title: Sonic Sancocho - Edición La Canícula — Sat Aug 22, 10:30 PM — Drom Taberna
item.description:
A parranda for La Canícula - the dog days of summer… we’re bringing the best tropical energy to celebrate the season.
Join us at Drom Taberna with performances by Soukustek and a hybrid PA performance / DJ set by local, Colombian-Canadian gem, David Ariza.
Our headlining band, Soukustek https://www.instagram.com/soukustek/ - comprised of Tury Morey and Claro Torres - gives us a taste of life growing up in Cartagena, Colombia, surrounded by African influences and Caribbean culture. Their vibrant, energetic performances paint bright portraits of heritage, enriched by movement and rhythm. The group's name combines Soukous (a popular Congolese dance music genre) and Champetex (a nod to Champeta, the Afro-Colombian musical culture deeply rooted in the Atlantic coast).
You know we always bring out the OGs… for this edition, we are thrilled to welcome David Ariza https://www.instagram.com/innerpeaceouterspace/ , who will deliver a signature soundscape between Soukoustek’s sets. David Ariza

item.title: Kensington Market Historical Society - Kensington's Jewish Roots: A Guided Tour — Sun Aug 30, 1:00 PM — Kensington Market
item.description:
Specially presented for attendees of the Ashkenaz Festival, this guided tour by the Kensington Market Historical Society (KMHS) bridges the gap between contemporary Yiddish culture and its deep-rooted heritage in Toronto. Taking place on Sunday, August 30, during the legendary Ashkenaz @ Pedestrian Sunday, this tour explores how early Eastern European Jewish immigrants built the bustling open-air market that set the stage for generations of Jewish arts, activism, and community. Discover the physical and cultural foundations of the neighbourhood before enjoying the festival’s afternoon performances. Start: Baldwin and Augusta Stage
Source: Ontario Historical Society
